entries.21e2b3ced89385f656592225c6c1cee508d3ca28:
The method allows granting the entity or natural person indicated in the request permissions to issue and/or view invoices within the composite context of the current context.  
            
The only way to identify the person being granted permissions is via the fingerprint of a qualified certificate:  
- electronic signature certificate for natural persons  
- electronic seal certificate for entities  
            
The request specifies the permissions to be granted from the following set:  
- **InvoiceWrite** – issuing invoices  
- **InvoiceRead** – viewing invoices  
            
The method allows selecting any combination of the above permissions.

> More information:
> - [Granting permissions](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-api/blob/main/uprawnienia.md#nadanie-uprawnie%C5%84-reprezentanta-podmiotu-unijnego)

entries.5b05735634bb94b26a143839d86649d98ca242b3:
The method allows reading permissions granted to a natural person or entity.  
 The list of retrieved permissions can be of two types:  
 - A list of all permissions applicable in the current login context (used when an administrator wants to review the permissions of all users in the current context)  
 - A list of all permissions granted in the current context by the authenticated API client (used when an administrator wants to review the list of permissions they have granted in the current context)  

 For the first list (applicable permissions), the response includes:  
 - persons and entities able to work in the current context, except for persons authorized indirectly  
 - persons authorized indirectly by the entity of the current context  

 For the second list (granted permissions), the response includes:  
 - permissions granted directly to work in the current context or in the context of subordinate units  
 - permissions granted indirectly to serve clients of the entity of the current context  

 Permissions returned by the operation include:  
 - **CredentialsManage** – managing permissions  
 - **CredentialsRead** – viewing permissions  
 - **InvoiceWrite** – issuing invoices  
 - **InvoiceRead** – viewing invoices  
 - **Introspection** – viewing session history  
 - **SubunitManage** – managing subordinate entities  
 - **EnforcementOperations** – performing enforcement operations  

 The response can be filtered based on the following parameters:  
 - **authorIdentifier** – identifier of the person who granted the permission  
 - **authorizedIdentifier** – identifier of the authorized person or entity  
 - **targetIdentifier** – identifier of the target entity for indirectly granted permissions  
 - **permissionTypes** – list of permission types to search for  
 - **permissionState** – permission status  
 - **queryType** – query type specifying which of the two lists is to be returned  

#### Result Pagination
The query returns **one page of results** with the number and size specified in the path.
- On the first call, set the parameter `pageOffset = 0`.  
- If another page of results is available, the **`hasMore`** flag will appear in the response.  
- In that case, the query can be called again with the next page number.

 > More information:
 > - [Retrieving the list of permissions](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-api/blob/main/uprawnienia.md#pobranie-listy-uprawnie%C5%84-do-pracy-w-ksef-nadanych-osobom-fizycznym-lub-podmiotom)

entries.6cffcb244be3d59eb1b142251a30f477f98583fa:
The method allows granting administrator permissions to the entity or natural person indicated in the request, in the context of:  
- the indicated NIP of a subordinate entity – exclusively if the entity of the current login context has the role of a parent entity:
  - **LocalGovernmentUnit** 
  - **VatGroupUnit**  
- the indicated or created internal identifier  
            
Along with the creation of the subordinate unit administrator, an internal identifier is created consisting of the NIP of the login context entity and 5 digits uniquely identifying the internal unit.
The last digit must be a valid check digit, which is calculated according to the algorithm below.

The algorithm uses alternating weights (1×, 3×, 1×, 3×, ...), sums the results and returns the remainder of division by 10.

Example:
- Input: "6824515772-1234" (without check digit)
- Position 0 (1st digit): 6 × 1 = 6
- Position 1 (2nd digit): 8 × 3 = 24
- Position 2 (3rd digit): 2 × 1 = 2
- Position 3 (4th digit): 4 × 3 = 12
- Position 4 (5th digit): 5 × 1 = 5
- Position 5 (6th digit): 1 × 3 = 3
- Position 6 (7th digit): 5 × 1 = 5
- Position 7 (8th digit): 7 × 3 = 21
- Position 8 (9th digit): 7 × 1 = 7
- Position 9 (10th digit): 2 × 3 = 6
- Position 10 (11th digit): 1 × 1 = 1
- Position 11 (12th digit): 2 × 3 = 6
- Position 12 (13th digit): 3 × 1 = 3
- Position 13 (14th digit): 4 × 3 = 12
- Sum: 6 + 24 + 2 + 12 + 5 + 3 + 5 + 21 + 7 + 6 + 1 + 6 + 3 + 12 = 113
- Check digit (15th digit): 113 % 10 = 3

The request also includes the name of this unit.  
            
Administrator permissions for the subordinate unit include:  
- **CredentialsManage** – credentials management  
            
The method automatically grants the above permission, without the need to specify it in the request.

A KSeF token is a unique, generated authenticating identifier that — on equal terms with a [qualified electronic signature](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-api/blob/main/uwierzytelnianie.md#21-uwierzytelnianie-kwalifikowanym-podpisem-elektronicznym) — enables [authentication](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-api/blob/main/uwierzytelnianie.md#22-uwierzytelnianie-tokenem-ksef) to the KSeF API. A KSeF token is issued with an immutable set of permissions defined at the time of its creation; any modification of these permissions requires generating a new token. > **Warning!**
> A KSeF token acts as a **confidential secret** for authentication — it must be stored exclusively in a trusted and secure vault. More information: - [KSeF token](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-api/blob/main/tokeny-ksef.md)

The method allows granting administrator permissions to the entity or natural person indicated in the request, within a context composed of the NIP identifier of the current context entity and the EU VAT number of the EU entity indicated in the request.  
Along with the creation of the EU entity administrator, a composite context is created consisting of the NIP number of the login context entity and the indicated EU VAT identification number of the EU entity.  
The request also includes the name and address of the EU entity.  
            
The only way to identify the person being granted permissions is via the fingerprint of a qualified certificate:  
- electronic signature certificate for natural persons  
- electronic seal certificate for entities  
            
EU entity administrator permissions include:  
- **VatEuManage** – managing permissions within the EU entity  
- **InvoiceWrite** – issuing invoices  
- **InvoiceRead** – viewing invoices  
- **Introspection** – viewing session history  
            
The method automatically grants all of the above permissions without the need to specify them in the request.
            
> More information:

The method allows reading the received permissions for invoice handling in the current login context.  

 The response includes the following permissions:  
 - granted to the entity for invoice handling by another entity 

 Permissions returned by the operation include:  
 - **InvoiceWrite** – issuing invoices  
 - **InvoiceRead** – viewing invoices  

 The response can be filtered based on the following parameters:  
 - **contextIdentifier** – identifier of the entity that granted the invoice handling permission  

#### Result pagination
The query returns **one page of results** with the number and size specified in the path.
- On the first call, set the parameter `pageOffset = 0`.  
- If another page of results is available, the **`hasMore`** flag will appear in the response.  
- In that case, the query can be called again with the next page number.
